How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

   Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the 2025 City Council meeting

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The most recent Material Demands from the Finance Department are presented

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve Material Demands as

  D. ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 24-68 DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER,
  FINANCE DIRECTOR, AND ASSISTANT FINANCE DIRECTOR AS
  AUTHORIZED AGENTS ON CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR’S OFFICE OF
  EMERGENCY SERVICES FORM 130

  In December 2022, the Finance Department submitted a project application
  requesting reimbursement for eligible COVID-19 expenditures that the City had
  incurred for emergency response services due to the COVID-19 Health
  Emergency. The California Office of Emergency Services (CalOES) requires the
  governing body to authorize by resolution, an agent to execute applications
  and contracts related to relief funds on CalOES Form 130. The approval and
  submission of CalOES Form 130 will enable the City to submit for
  reimbursement from disaster relief funds. The Designation of Applicant’s Agent
  Resolutions for Non-State Agencies is valid for three years. There is no Fiscal
  Impact as a result of the adoption of Resolution No. 24-68, designating
  authorized agents with respect to applications for state and federal financial
  assistance for disasters.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-68
  designating the City Manager, Finance Director, and Assistant Finance Director

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2024  3
   as the Authorized Agents for the State of California Governor’s Office of
  Emergency Services to execute for and on behalf of the City of San Gabriel to
  obtain federal financial assistance for existing and future grant programs.

  E. AWARD OF CONTRACT  FOR  NEW  RECREATION  MANAGEMENT
  SOFTWARE PROVIDER

  At the June 4, 2024 City Council Meeting, Council approved the Fiscal Year
  2024-2025 budget, which included funds allocated for the purchase of new
  recreation management software. The recreations management software will
  be used for all Community Services Division functions as well as processing
  payments for parking and concessions for the Mission Playhouse Division. Staff
  released a request for proposals on September 13, 2024, and received eight
  proposals. Of those, three were selected for an interview. The implementation
  and first-year-cost would be $26,422 directly to CivicPlus, with an additional
  one-time cost of $3,803.63 to purchase six credit card readers to CardConnect.
  Funding for this agreement and the purchase of the credit card readers is
  included in the proposed Fiscal Year 2024-2025 operating budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the professional services agreement for recreation management software
  services with CivicPlus, LLC.

  F. APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT WITH ECO SYSTEMS IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $30,000 PLUS A $6,000 CONTINGENCY FOR THE ROOFING REPAIR AT
  SMITH PARK POOL [RESOLUTION NO. 24-67]

  The existing roof at Smith Park Pool is more than 20 years old and is in need of
  roofing repairs due to severe leaking. Public Works staff contacted professional
  roofing companies to obtain quotes for the roof repair. The lowest responsive
  bidder for Smith Park Pool Roof Repair is Eco Systems. Staff has requested
  approval from Los Angeles County Regional Park and Open Space District
  (RPOSD) to use the City’s allocation for this project. It is anticipated that RPOSD
  will approve the expenditure which will cover the project costs. In order to move
  forward with this project, staff is requesting an appropriation of $36,000 (repair
  costs plus contingency) to cover the required project budget for the roofing
  work at Smith Park Pool.

City Council Special Meeting Agenda – December 3, 2024  4
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  project as defined in Section 15378 of the state CEQA Guidelines, as re-roofing of
  existing roof at Smith Park Pool does not reasonably create a possibility that the
  work will have any significant impacts to the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a contract with Eco Systems in the amount of $30,000 plus a contingency of
  $6,000 using account number 122-850-15-97-608 (Smith Park Pool Facility
  Roof Repair/Replacement). Additionally, Staff recommends the City Council
  adopt Resolution No. 24-67 to appropriate $36,000 from the General Fund to
  account number 122-850-15-97-608 for the above-mentioned project.

  G. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-70 AMENDING THE 2024-2025
  BUDGET TO ADD $10,500 TO THE SISTER CITY ITEM LINE, AND APPROVAL
  OF CITY-PAID TRAVEL EXPENSES TO TAIWAN (REPUBLIC OF CHINA) TO
  SELECT LANTERNS FOR THE 2026 SAN GABRIEL LUNAR LANTERN
  FESTIVAL AND TO VISIT SAN GABRIEL SITER CITY OF BANQIAO DISTRICT,
  NEW TAIPEI CITY

  The City has an agreement with the Taiwan Tourism Administration (TTA) for
  the donation of lanterns for ten years to support San Gabriel’s annual Lunar
  Lantern Festival. The TTA has invited representatives from the City to travel to
  Taoyuan, Taiwan (Republic of China (R.O.C.) to be guests at the 2025 Taiwan
  Lantern Festival and choose lanterns for donation to San Gabriel for our 2026
  Lunar Lantern Festival. In addition, Taoyuan is adjacent to New Taipei City,
  which is home to one of San Gabriel’s current Sister Cities, Banqiao District. The
  trip would also allow San Gabriel representatives to meet with government
  officials and civic leaders in Banqiao District. The fiscal impact of the trip to
  Taiwan is estimated to be $10,500. The Sister City budget line item is insufficient
  to fund the trip, requiring funds to be allocated from the General Fund balance.
  Approval of Resolution No. 24-70 authorizes adding $10,500 to the Sister City
  line item in the 2024-2025 budget.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-70 amending
  the 2024-2025 budget and approve City-paid expenses for a trip to Taiwan for
  the Mayor and City Manager.

MINUTES OF DECEMBER 3, 2024
  SPECIAL MEETING OF THE SAN GABRIEL CITY COUNCIL

I  CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Wu called the special meeting of the San Gabriel City Council to order at 7:33 P.M.
  on Tuesday, December 3, 2024, in the Council Chamber at City Hall, 425 South Mission
  Drive, San Gabriel, California, 91776.

  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Council Member Harrington.

  ROLL CALL

  Council Members Present:  Eric Chan, Tony Ding, John R. Harrington, Vice Mayor
  Menchaca, and Mayor John Wu.
  Council Members Absent:  None.
  Staff Members Present:  City Manager Mark Lazzaretto, Assistant City Attorney
  Martin Koczanowicz, Fire Chief Steven Wallace, Human

I  Resources/Risk Management Director Edward Macias,
  Finance Director William Kaholokula, Community
  Development Director Aldo Cervantes, Police Chief
  Edward Elizalde, Acting Public Works Director Szeka
  Cheng, Assistant Community Services Director Matthew
  Morales-Stevens, and Assistant City Clerk Marilyn
  Bonus.

  ANNOUNCEMENTS

  Assistant City Clerk Bonus provided information for the public on how to view the
  meeting.

  1. APPROVAL OF AGENDA ORDER

  Hearing no objection, Mayor Wu approved the Agenda Order.

  2. PRESENTATIONS

I  A. EMPLOYEE AWARDS AND RECOGNITION

  City Manager Lazzaretto made the presentation.

  3. PUBLIC COMMENT

  Chloe Dang, resident, commented on the benefits of diversity in San Gabriel and
  proposed the creation of a committee to explore the logistics of creating a minority
  business accelerator in the City.

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 1 of 4  December 3, 2024
   4. CONSENT CALENDAR

  Staff requested that Item 4F be approved as amended to change the company name
  from Roofing Plus Construction, Inc., to Eco Systems in the first WHEREAS of
  Resolution No. 24-67.

  Council Member Chan pulled Item 4G for separate discussion.

  A motion was made by Council Member Chan, seconded by Vice Mayor Menchaca, to

I  approve Consent Calendar Items 4A - 4E as presented, and 4F as amended.

  Motion carried by a vote of 5-0 as follows:

  AYES:  CHAN, DING, HARRINGTON, MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  NONE
  ABSTAIN:  NONE
  ABSENT:  NONE

  Regarding Item 4G, discussion included the existing policy that excludes travel costs
  from being funded by the City; travel cost as an investment to build good will; fiduciary
  duty to the residents; benefits to the City of receiving lanterns through the Sister City
  program; benefits to the City of City Manager Lazzaretto traveling to Taiwan; value of
  and balancing benefits to each party; clarification that travel expenses would be only
  for the City Manager; clarification that any donation or reimbursement of travel
  expenses should be given to the City, not to an individual, and relevant findings that
  must be present; and travel budget as part of a Sister City policy.

  A motion was made by Vice Mayor Menchaca, seconded by Mayor Wu, to adopt

I  Resolution No. 24-70 as amended, to amend the 2024-2025 budget to approve City-
  paid expenses for a trip to Taiwan for the City Manager in the amount of $5,500.

  Motion failed by a vote of 2-2- 7 as follows:

  AYES:  MENCHACA, WU
  NOES:  CHAN, HARRINGTON
  ABSTAIN:  DING
  ABSENT:  NONE

  A. APPROVAL OF MINUTES

  The City Council approved the following:

  1. Minutes of the Special City Council Meeting of November 19, 2024.
  2. Minutes of the Regular City Council Meeting of November 19, 2024.

  B. 2025 CITY COUNCIL MEETING SCHEDULE

I  The City Council approved the 2025 City Council meeting schedule.

  C. MATERIAL DEMANDS

  The City Council approved November 8 and 15, 2024, Material Demands for the
  payment of City expenditures.

  D. ADOPT RESOLUTION NO. 24-68 DESIGNATING THE CITY MANAGER,
  FINANCE DIRECTOR, AND ASSISTANT FINANCE DIRECTOR AS AUTHORIZED

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 2 of 4  December 3, 2024
   AGENTS ON CALIFORNIA GOVERNOR'S OFFICE OF EMERGENCY SERVICES
  FORM 130

  The City Council adopted Resolution No. 24-68 designating the City Manager,
  Finance Director, and Assistant Finance Director as the Authorized Agents for the
  State of California Governor's Office of Emergency Services to execute for and on
  behalf of the City of San Gabriel to obtain federal financial assistance for existing
  and future grant programs.

I
  E. AWARD OF CONTRACT FOR NEW RECREATION MANAGEMENT SOFTWARE
  PROVIDER

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute the professional services
  agreement for recreation management software services with CivicPlus, LLC.

  F. APPROVAL OF A CONTRACT WITH ECO SYSTEMS IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $30,000 PLUS A $6,000 CONTINGENCY FOR THE ROOFING REPAIR AT SMITH
  PARK POOL [RESOLUTION NO. 24-67]

  The City Council authorized the City Manager to execute a contract with Eco
  Systems in the amount of $30,000 plus a contingency of $6,000 using account
  number 122-850-15-97-608 (Smith Park Pool Facility Roof Repair/Replacement);
  and adopted Resolution No. 24-67 to appropriate $36,000 from the General Fund
  to account number 122-850-15-97-608 for the above-mentioned project, as
  amended to change the company name from Roofing Plus Construction, Inc., to
  Eco Systems in the first WHEREAS of the Resolution.

  G. ADOPTION OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-70 AMENDING THE 2024-2025 BUDGET

I  TO ADD $10,500 TO THE SISTER CITY ITEM LINE, AND APPROVAL OF CITY-
  PAID TRAVEL EXPENSES TO TAIWAN (REPUBLIC OF CHINA) TO SELECT
  LANTERNS FOR THE 2026 SAN GABRIEL LUNAR LANTERN FESTIVAL AND TO
  VISIT SAN GABRIEL SITER CITY OF BANQIAO DISTRICT, NEW TAIPEI CITY

  This item was not approved .

  5. PUBLIC HEARING - None.

  6. CONTINUED BUSINESS - None.

  7. NEW BUSINESS - None.

  8. PUBLIC COMMENT - None.

  9. CITY MANAGER'S REPORT

  City Manager Lazzaretto recognized former Public Works Director/City Engineer Greg
  de Vinck for his years of service to the City and commented that many of the employee

I  award recipients were beneficiaries of his tutelage.

  The City Council highly-commended Mr. de Vinck's service to the City and wished him
  well in his new position as Public Works Director for the City of Pasadena.

  10. COUNCIL COMMENTS AND CONFERENCE/MEETING REPORTS

  Council Member Chan reported on his attendance at Rosemead's Public Safety Center
  remodel groundbreaking event and a San Gabriel Historical Association dinner

  CITY COUNCIL SPECIAL MEETING MINUTES  Page 3 of 4  December 3, 2024
   fundraiser; and commended the great job by the Community Services Department on
  City events.

  Council Member Ding reported on his attendance at the Mosque's food distribution
  to seniors, Rosemead Public Safety station event, San Gabriel Historical Association
  dinner, and San Gabriel's holiday tree-lighting event.

  Vice Mayor Menchaca reported on her attendance at the City's holiday tree-lighting
  event and made suggestions for future enhancements, and commended La Casa and

I  Mosque food donations.

  Council Member Harrington requested that the City add pie tin decorations by
  children to the tree-lighting event.

  Mayor Wu reported on his attendance at the Haka Federation of USA event for seniors
  and Southern California Council of Chinese Schools award ceremony.

  11. CLOSED SESSION - None.

  12. ADJOURNMENT

  The meeting was adjourned at 9:00 P.M.

  Respectfully submitted:

I
  Approved this 17th day of December, 2024:

  JO~

I
